newsitem.title: UK: Lights go out for UK Conservatives on Muckle Flugga.
newsitem.headline: Lights go out for UK Conservatives on Muckle Flugga.

text.p: The boast sounded too good to be true -- and maybe it was.

Prime Minister John Major was proudly told on Wednesday by his Conservative Party's candidate for the northernmost seat in Britain that the whole of Scotland was swinging behind him -- including the rocky outcrop of Muckle Flugga, home to a lighthouse and not much more.
"I've actually visted Muckle Flugga at the very northerly tip of Scotland," Hope Anderson told Major on a video link to Inverness where the prime minister was campaigning.
"Muckle Flugga is now electrified and the lighthouse keeper of Muckle Flugga is a Conservative. Scotland is Conservative from its very tip to its very bottom," he said.
Major beamed and said although he wasn't sure he could pronounce it, he would visit Muckle Flugga once he had won next Thursday's election.
But by the time the prime minister had reached Fochabers an hour to the south to tour a soup factory, questions were being raised.

Contacted by mobile telephone, one of Muckle Flugga's last two lightkeepers said the island had been uninhabited since the lighthouse was automated in 1995. Now it was home only to puffins, gannets and seals.
What's more, Ron Bernie, said, there was "no way" he would vote Conservative on May 1. "I've never supported them," he said.
Bernie, who lives alone on the island of Bressay about 35 miles (56 km) south of Muckle Flugga, voted at the 1992 election for the Liberal Democrats, who won the seat of Orkney and Shetlands.
This time round, he says he's not sure he'll vote at all.
"I'm fed up with all these politicians. They're on the television until midnight. You can't get away from them," he said.
Asked whether he agreed Scotland was Conservative from top to bottom, Bernie said: "Not at the moment. There's no one at the tip."
